run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: checkout is unavailable because its Deployment's pod template carries a nodeSelector (kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node) that matches none of the cluster's four nodes, so every replacement checkout pod stays Pending/Unschedulable. The previously serving pod checkout-6c769b88b5-sxm5l had started its checkout container at 16:40:12Z and was killed at 16:40:40Z; the two ReplicaSets created immediately afterwards (checkout-54579c864c at 16:40:40Z, checkout-c69887c97 at 16:40:46Z) both use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-checkout, both carry the extra-node nodeSelector, and neither has a ready replica. With zero ready checkout replicas, the checkout Service 10.96.132.210:8080 has an Endpoints object with no subsets and calls to it are refused: frontend POST /api/checkout returns HTTP 500 with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE and 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.132.210:8080'. Observed impact is confined to that path: at 16:40:57Z locust_requests_num_failures is 0 for every endpoint except POST /api/checkout (2 failures, aggregate fail ratio 0.133), and at the 16:40:45Z sample kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready is 1 for all 23 other astronomy-shop deployments and 0 for checkout. The checkout path itself worked before the rollout (a checkout PlaceOrder server span at 16:40:34.166Z returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0 under a frontend POST /api/checkout with HTTP 200, and that trace's payment, cart, currency, shipping, email and product-catalog calls all succeeded), and every flagd fault flag is at defaultVariant off, so neither a checkout application fault nor a dependency or flag-driven fault is supported. The root cause object is Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop.

claims.text: Deployment checkout (astronomy-shop) has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}, no node affinity and no tolerations, while the cluster's only nodes are sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3 - none named extra-node.

Deployment checkout status shows no ready replica: spec.replicas=1 but status.replicas=2, unavailableReplicas=2 and condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability.').
checkout is the only deployment in astronomy-shop with a nodeSelector: all the other 22 deployments return nodeSelector null and nodeAffinity null.

Both current checkout pods are Pending with condition PodScheduled=False reason Unschedulable: '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.', and each pod's own spec.nodeSelector is {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}.

The two ReplicaSets owned by Deployment checkout, checkout-54579c864c (created 2026-11-21T16:40:40Z) and checkout-c69887c97 (created 2026-11-21T16:40:46Z), both use the unchanged image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-checkout and both carry nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}; each has 1 desired replica, 1 status replica and no ready replicas.

Service checkout is ClusterIP 10.96.132.210, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout, and the Endpoints object named checkout has no subsets (no ready addresses), so connections to it are refused.

Deployment checkout rollout events: pod checkout-6c769b88b5-sxm5l was Scheduled to sregym-worker3 at 16:39:42Z, its checkout container Started at 16:40:12Z and was stopped ('Stopping container checkout') at 16:40:40Z; the Deployment then scaled up checkout-54579c864c at 16:40:40Z (its pod checkout-54579c864c-b5sv5 logged FailedScheduling at 16:40:40Z) and checkout-c69887c97 at 16:40:46Z (its pod checkout-c69887c97-25jw4 logged FailedScheduling at 16:40:46Z).

frontend spans for the failing requests show POST /api/checkout with http.status_code=500 and error=true, client span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code=14, and tcp.connect spans whose error detail is 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.132.210:8080' / '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.132.210:8080 (2026-11-21T16:40:46.806Z)'; the same traces' frontend-proxy ('POST', 'router frontend egress') and load-generator ('POST') spans also carry HTTP 500.
Pod frontend-6859c775df-bxzrj logged 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.132.210:8080' at 16:40:03Z, 16:40:09Z, 16:40:46Z and 16:40:47Z.

At the 16:40:45Z sample kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready is 0 for deployment checkout and 1 for each of the other 23 astronomy-shop deployments (including payment, cart, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog, kafka, valkey-cart), and a point query at 16:40:50Z also returns 0 for checkout.
At 16:40:57Z locust_requests_num_failures is 0 for every endpoint except POST /api/checkout, which reads 2, the Aggregated series reads 2, and locust_requests_fail_ratio is 0.1333.

Immediately before the rollout the checkout path succeeded: a checkout server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder starting 16:40:34.166Z has rpc.grpc.status_code=0, its frontend POST /api/checkout parents have http.status_code=200, and the same trace's payment oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (19.459ms), cart, currency, shipping, email and product-catalog spans returned status 0 or HTTP 200.

The terminated checkout pod's logs (Loki, pod checkout-6c769b88b5-sxm5l, 16:39:46Z-16:40:11Z) contain only wait-for-kafka init-container lines ending with 'kafka (10.96.161.91:9092) open' at 16:40:11.75Z; no application error line from the checkout container appears in the returned lines.

The checkout Deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration embeds the same pod template, including "nodeSelector":{"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-checkout, and the live object is at generation 2 / observedGeneration 2 with rollout conditions last changing at 16:40:40Z and 16:40:46Z.

ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has every fault-injection flag at defaultVariant 'off' - paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse - so an enabled flagd fault is not supported by the observed configuration.

The Endpoints objects for the neighbouring services cart (10.244.234.148, sregym-worker), payment (10.244.7.218, sregym-worker2) and valkey-cart (10.244.234.178, sregym-worker) all have ready addresses, while only checkout has none, so the refusal is specific to checkout rather than namespace-wide.

Rejected: node capacity or taint exhaustion. All four nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, 8 CPU and 110 pods allocatable, the only taint is the control-plane NoSchedule, and every other astronomy-shop pod is Running and ready; the scheduler message names node affinity/selector mismatch, not insufficient resources.

Rejected: checkout application failure or crash. The checkout server span at 16:40:34.166Z returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, the terminated checkout pod's retrieved lines show no application error, and the two current checkout pods have no containerStatuses at all because they were never scheduled - the failure is scheduling, not the checkout process.

The rollout at about 16:40:40Z replaced the checkout pod template with one carrying nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node while reusing the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-checkout, consistent with a configuration-only change; no chaos or fault-injection object declaring that change was observed, so the actor remains unknown.

Remove the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node from Deployment checkout (or point it at an existing node such as sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 or sregym-worker3), then confirm new checkout pods reach Running/Ready, the checkout Endpoints object regains an address, and POST /api/checkout stops returning 500 in locust and traces.

gaps: The actor and exact instant of the Deployment change could not be observed: change_history is not integrated, and no mutating webhook configuration was returned (that query returned no items), so only the Deployment's last-applied annotation, generation/conditions and the 16:40:40Z / 16:40:46Z rollout events bound the change in time.

The ResourceQuota and NetworkPolicy queries for astronomy-shop both returned no_data (0 items), so their absence is that query's result only, not a proven fact; resource quotas and network policies therefore remain unchecked and unexcluded as alternative causes.

Prometheus returned no samples anywhere in the window for traces_span_metrics_calls_total, traces_* metric names, rpc_*/http_server_* metric names, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready range queries over longer spans, and locust_requests_num_failures as a range - the corresponding queries returned no_data, so span-based error-rate and latency trends could not be measured and no latency baseline exists.

Application logs for the two Pending checkout pods could not be read (containers never started; fetch_pod_logs returned SOURCE_ERROR for checkout-c69887c97-25jw4), and the deleted pod checkout-6c769b88b5-sxm5l no longer exists in the Kubernetes API (POD_NOT_FOUND), so only its Loki init-container lines were retrievable, not its checkout container stdout.

The ALERTS query at 16:40:57Z returned no_data, and the alert-rules listing has no time range, so which alert (if any) opened this investigation and when the failure signal first deviated are unknown.
Kubernetes events in the returned data only reach back to about 16:39:42Z, so namespace activity before that is unknown, and the 24h authorized window earlier than that is unsampled for events.
Whether callers other than load-generator/frontend were calling checkout, and any customer impact beyond the observed POST /api/checkout 500s, is unverified.
next_steps: Correct the checkout Deployment's nodeSelector to a node hostname that exists (or drop it), then watch checkout pod scheduling, the checkout Endpoints object, and POST /api/checkout success until locust_requests_num_failures for /api/checkout returns to 0.
Add an alert on kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{deployment="checkout"} == 0 and on pods stuck in PodScheduled=False / FailedScheduling, since no firing alert was visible at the sampled instant.

Enable or repair OTLP span-metrics export (traces_span_metrics_*, rpc_*_duration_*, http_server_request_duration_seconds_*) for this environment so error-rate and latency can be measured directly next time.
Confirm from change history or CI/Helm values who introduced nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node on the checkout Deployment and when.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
